newsitem.title: FRANCE: Generale says Cinven deal 8.5 bln Ffr.
newsitem.headline: Generale says Cinven deal 8.5 bln Ffr.

text.p: French conglomerate Generale des Eaux, confirming the sale of its health activities to Cinven Ltd of Britain, said the deal valued its Generale de Sante unit at "slightly over 8.5 billion francs" in French currency terms.
The group said in a brief statement it would retain a 20 percent shareholding in Generale de Sante France after the deal.
Cinven, a British fund management firm, said earlier it had bought the health activities of Generale des Eaux in a deal which it valued at 1.1 billion pounds ($1.8 billion).

Cinven is organising what it called the largest European management buyout of the decade, which will see the managements of General des Eaux's two businesses Generale de Sante in France and General Healthcare Group in the UK buy the businesses from Cinven.
Generale des Eaux outperformed a buoyant French stock market to trade 1.06 percent higher at 763 francs per share at 0922 GMT. The CAC-40 blue-chip index was 0.72 percent higher.
